servers.name: Plex
servers.source: jimbo-dj's database, read-only (its last Plex sync)

servers.name: Jellyfin
servers.note: Not set up: TRAQFREQ_JELLYFIN_URL, TRAQFREQ_JELLYFIN_KEY missing. Every page works without it.

refresh.rule: POST /api/servers/{server}/refresh: GET requests to the server only; writes traqfreq's own database (its snapshot and this log), nothing else.

servers.name: Navidrome
servers.note: Not set up: TRAQFREQ_NAVIDROME_URL, TRAQFREQ_NAVIDROME_USER, TRAQFREQ_NAVIDROME_PASSWORD missing. Every page works without it.

refresh.rule: POST /api/servers/{server}/refresh: GET requests to the server only; writes traqfreq's own database (its snapshot and this log), nothing else.

/api/servers.read_only: traqfreq never writes to any server: GET requests only, no playlists, plays or tags.

/api/servers/identity.root_rule: jimbo-dj's music folders (its PATH_MAP, as stored in library.stats paths.folders)

rules.copies: Live tracks in jimbo-dj's database (removed_at IS NULL): one Plex copy each, keyed by rating_key.
rules.with_file: Copies with a file key: Plex gives a path and it is inside one of Plex's music folders. The file key is the path below that folder (Unicode NFC, / separators, case kept).
rules.files: Distinct file keys among the copies.
rules.songs: Songs as jimbo-dj counts them (songs.py): track artist (else album artist) and title without the version, so a live take and the album track are one song.
rules.songs_with_versions: Songs with more than one copy in the library.
rules.match_keys: Distinct listen match keys (history.py: normalised artist|title) among the copies.
rules.no_path: Plex gives no file for the copy (plex_path is empty). No other server can be matched by file.
rules.outside_roots: The file is outside every Plex music folder, so it has no file key.
rules.shared_file: Two or more live copies point at one file. They will match the same item on another server.
rules.loose_clash: Two different file keys that are equal once case-folded: on a case-insensitive disk they would be one file, so the loose key can't decide between them.
rules.multi_part: Plex joins two or more files into this copy and jimbo-dj keeps only the first part's path. The other parts may be items of their own on Jellyfin and Navidrome.
rules.no_duration: Plex gives no duration, so the tag tier (durations within 2 s) can't use the copy.

tiers.rule: The same file key; then the same loose key when only one item has it.
The same MusicBrainz recording and release, from the server's tags.
The same match key, album, disc and track number, durations within 2 s; only when exactly one candidate is left.

snapshots.folder_rule: the folder every real path shares (the server names no folder paths)

rules.matched: Copies matched to one jellyfin item, at the tier said.
rules.items_matched: Distinct jellyfin items matched (a shared file counts once).
rules.copies_unmatched: Not matched; each with one reason, so the reasons add up to this.
rules.items_unmatched: jellyfin items nothing matched; each with one reason.
rules.file: The same file key (the path below each server's music folder); then the same loose key (case-folded), only when exactly one item has it.
rules.mbid: The same MusicBrainz recording and release, from the server's tags. A Plex copy has none of its own: it uses the IDs of the item its file matched on the other server.
rules.tags: The same match key (artist|title, normalised as listens are), album, disc and track number, and durations within 2 s; only when exactly one candidate is left.
rules.loose: Matched by the loose key: the file key with other capitals.
rules.shared_file: Two or more Plex copies point at one file; they all match its one item.
rules.multi_part: A multi-part Plex copy, matched by its first part's file.

rules.items_matched: Distinct navidrome items matched (a shared file counts once).

rules.items_unmatched: navidrome items nothing matched; each with one reason.

rules.loose: Matched by the loose key: the file key with other capitals.
rules.shared_file: Two or more Plex copies point at one file; they all match its one item.
rules.multi_part: A multi-part Plex copy, matched by its first part's file.

reasons.no_path: No file to match by: Plex gives no path for the copy, or the server none for the item; the MusicBrainz and tag tiers found nothing either.
reasons.outside_roots: The file is outside the known music folders, so it has no file key; the MusicBrainz and tag tiers found nothing either.
reasons.not_on_server: No item on the other server has this file, MusicBrainz IDs or tags.
reasons.ambiguous: More than one candidate at the first tier that had any (or one candidate two copies want): traqfreq doesn't guess.
reasons.hidden_path: The server gives no real path (Navidrome without Report Real Path), so the file tier can't be used, and the MusicBrainz and tag tiers found nothing.
reasons.not_in_plex: An item no Plex copy matched: a file Plex doesn't list.
reasons.multi_part: Another part of a multi-part Plex copy (same folder, disc and track): Plex keeps only the first part's file, which is matched; this part is not.

rules.plays: max(Plex view_count, history plays), never the sum (jimbo-dj's plays_of)
rules.history: counted listens of this copy: COALESCE(listens.rating_key, listen_matches.rating_key) = it (jimbo-dj's _track_stats; on a song with more copies, pages.song's version history)
rules.song_history: counted listens of every copy of the song (pages._keys_where over its versions)
rules.versions: other live copies of the same song: the same artist (track artist first) and title without its version, like (Live) or - Remastered (songs.Index)
rules.analysis: jimbo-dj's analyzer: analysis.status and version (current = ok at version 2); key, BPM and moods from its features row
rules.sources: counted listens per source, in jimbo-dj's source order
rules.years: counted listens per year, in the listening time zone

tiers.rule: The same file key (the path below each server's music folder); then the same loose key (case-folded), only when exactly one item has it.
The same MusicBrainz recording and release, from the server's tags. A Plex copy has none of its own: it uses the IDs of the item its file matched on the other server.
The same match key (artist|title, normalised as listens are), album, disc and track number, and durations within 2 s; only when exactly one candidate is left.
Jellyfin ↔ Navidrome: both items are matched to the same Plex copy.

reasons.no_path: No file to match by: Plex gives no path for the copy, or the server none for the item; the MusicBrainz and tag tiers found nothing either.
reasons.outside_roots: The file is outside the known music folders, so it has no file key; the MusicBrainz and tag tiers found nothing either.
reasons.not_on_server: No item on the other server has this file, MusicBrainz IDs or tags.
reasons.ambiguous: More than one candidate at the first tier that had any (or one candidate two copies want): traqfreq doesn't guess.
reasons.hidden_path: The server gives no real path (Navidrome without Report Real Path), so the file tier can't be used, and the MusicBrainz and tag tiers found nothing.
reasons.not_in_plex: An item no Plex copy matched: a file Plex doesn't list.
reasons.multi_part: Another part of a multi-part Plex copy (same folder, disc and track): Plex keeps only the first part's file, which is matched; this part is not.
